newsitem.title: MAURITIUS: Mauritius fin min vows strong rupee policy.
newsitem.headline: Mauritius fin min vows strong rupee policy.

text.p: Mauritian Finance Minister Vasant Bunwaree has pledged a strong rupee policy to create an environment conducive for investments and halt purchasing power erosion in the Indian Ocean island.

"Among the crucial elements (of the economy), I can say there will be a strategic centre and all the rest will orbit around that centre. That's what I call a strong rupee," Bunwaree said during a gathering with trade unions late on Wednesday.
"If we do not follow a strong rupee policy, I do not think we will be able to attain these (economic) objectives."
Bunwaree said he targetted medium term economic growth of 5.5 percent and 6.5 percent per annum over the next three years and inflation below five percent by the end of the century.
The latest inflation estimate for calendar 1996 has been posted at 6.6 percent from 6.0 percent in 1995.
Bunwaree also aimed at raising the level of investments in the economy to 30 percent of gross domestic product (GDP) by the year 2000 from a present 24.5 percent of GDP.

When Bunwaree was appointed finance minister on November 27, the rupee was trading at a mean commercial rate of 20.0965 against the dollar. It was quoted at a mean rate of 19.9505 for one dollar during Wednesday's fixing.
